name: Winter Storm Prep
title: Winter Storm Prep Gear: Radios, Food, Water & Ice Essentials
summary: The basics to ride out a snow or ice storm at home: weather radios, shelf-stable food, water, and traction.
intro: Ice storms and blizzards can cut roads and power for days. This lane covers the core supplies that matter most when you're stuck at home: a way to hear alerts, food and water that don't need a fridge, and gear to move around safely on ice.

name: Power Outage Kits
title: Power Outage Kit Essentials: Lights, Energy Reserves & Safety
summary: Lanterns, headlamps, portable energy reserves, and safety gear for when the grid goes down.
intro: When the lights go out, the first hours are about light, communication, and keeping key devices charged. These picks cover hands-free lighting, rechargeable backup power, and the safety gear that prevents outage emergencies from getting worse.

name: Vehicle Emergency Kits
title: Winter Vehicle Emergency Kit: Jump Starters, Scrapers & Warmth
summary: What to keep in your car or truck: jump starters, snow brushes, blankets, first aid, and a way to call for help.
intro: Cold weather drains batteries and strands drivers. A small, well-chosen kit in the trunk turns a dangerous wait into an inconvenience. Start with the items here, then see our guide to what to keep in your car for winter.

name: Home Heating Backup
title: Backup Heat for Power Outages: Indoor-Safe Heaters & CO Safety
summary: Indoor-rated portable heaters and the carbon monoxide alarms you need alongside them.
intro: Losing heat in a winter outage is serious. Only use heaters rated for indoor use, follow the manufacturer's ventilation instructions, and always run a working carbon monoxide alarm. Never use a grill, camp stove, or generator indoors.

name: Cold-Weather Gear
title: Cold-Weather Gear: Warm Socks, Hand Warmers & Ice Traction
summary: Personal warmth and footing: wool socks, rechargeable hand warmers, and ice cleats.
intro: Staying warm starts with what you wear. Wool layers, rechargeable hand warmers, and traction for icy steps help whether you're shoveling the driveway, checking livestock, or walking to the mailbox.

name: Off-Grid Power
title: Off-Grid Power: Solar Panels & Energy Reserves
summary: Solar panels and battery energy reserves for cabins, RVs, job sites, and long outages.
intro: Energy reserves paired with solar panels can recharge during multi-day outages and keep running at camp, on the job site, or at the hunting cabin. Match the panel connector and input limits to your energy reserve before you buy.

name: Storm & Hurricane Prep
title: Storm & Hurricane Prep: Water, Food Storage & Grab-and-Go Kits
summary: For hurricane and severe-storm season: water filtration, cold storage, and go-bags.
intro: Hurricanes and severe storms bring long outages and boil-water notices. These picks focus on safe drinking water, keeping food cold, and having a bag ready if you need to leave.

name: Homestead & Multi-Purpose
title: Homestead & Multi-Purpose Tools: Multi-Tools, Cast Iron & More
summary: Tools that earn their keep every day and in emergencies: multi-tools, cast iron, and versatile cookers.
intro: The best preparedness gear is gear you use every week. Multi-tools, cast iron, and portable cookers work just as well for chores and cookouts as they do when the power is out.

name: Home Backup Power & Solar
title: Inverter Generator vs Energy Reserve & Solar for Outages
summary: Compare inverter generators, portable energy reserves, and solar panels for hurricane and everyday power outages.
intro: When the lights go out, the usual choice is an inverter generator, a portable energy reserve, or both, with solar to recharge when the grid is down. This lane gathers real generators, battery energy reserves, and portable panels for home backup. Gas generators must be used only outdoors, more than 20 feet from windows, doors, and vents, with a working carbon monoxide alarm inside, following the manufacturer's ventilation instructions.

name: Water & Food Storage
title: Emergency Water Filters vs Straw Filters, Plus Food Storage
summary: Emergency water filters versus straw filters, plus water storage and hurricane food that needs no refrigeration.
intro: Before a hurricane or long outage, store enough water and shelf-stable food, and have a way to treat more water if a boil-water notice lasts. This lane covers storage containers, gravity and bottle filters, straw-style filters, and long-shelf meals. Ready.gov recommends storing at least one gallon of water per person per day for several days, for drinking and sanitation.

name: First Aid & Medical Prep
title: Family First Aid Kits for Storms, Outages, and Medical Prep
summary: What to put in a family first aid kit for storms, plus medical-prep supplies to keep at home during an outage.
intro: A storm kit should include a family first aid kit and the personal medical items your household actually uses. This lane collects organized kits, bleeding-control and splint supplies, and an AED option. This is not medical advice. Follow Red Cross, CDC, or manufacturer guidance, get first-aid training, and call 911 in an emergency.
